rationale:
Iteration 10 (base_speed 1.4, kd 0.8) scored 192.9, below the 255.7 of iteration 6. Oval finishes fell from 9 of 20 to 4 of 20, so the stated rule applies: return base_speed to 1.3 on the iteration 6 design. I apply that rule and change nothing else.

Why this design: iteration 6 is the best raced state (255.7, oval finishes 9 of 20, line_loss 0, oval mean finish time 1.89 s, oval max_error 0.0535 m). Every later single-variable test came out lower: y = 0.01 m (179.1), ki 0.15 (253.2, no change in max_error), kd 0.5 (56.8, finishes collapsed), base_speed 1.4 (192.9). Iteration 6 is therefore the only measured design with a known good result, and this is the final iteration, so there is no later race to recover from a bad candidate. Only the candidate itself is raced on the unseen track.

Geometry: 7 line sensors at y = 0.03 m, x = -0.06 to +0.06 m in 0.02 m steps, sensor size 0.012 m, wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg. Controller: base_speed 1.3, kp 5.0, ki 0.02, kd 0.8, weights [-1, -0.75, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1], line_loss last_direction.

Expected result: about 9 of 20 oval finishes with line_loss 0. The unseen track is the main uncertainty, since the s-bend and slalom have never been finished in any design. Hypotheses: (a) the 1.3 speed setting holds on a different shape; (b) max_error stays near 0.06 m on tight bends, which limits finishes. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events and steering oscillation.
